item.title: Thundercat Announces First New LP in Six Years
item.description: R&amp;B pioneer Thundercat is finally preparing to release his follow-up album to 2020's It Is What It Is. His next LP is titled Distracted, and is set to be dropped April 3.

item.title: Super Bowl 2026 Music Recap: Bad Bunny, Green Day, Charlie Puth &amp; More Perform
item.description: Bad Bunny's halftime show, as well as other acts such as Green Day, Coco Jones, Brandi Carlile, Charlie Puth, Lady Gaga, and Ricky Martin unified the crowd at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California.

item.title: Britney Spears Sells Rights to Her Music Catalogue
item.description: Pop legend Britney Spears recently sold the rights to her entire music catalogue. The news was first broken by TMZ this week (February 10), followed by subsequent reports from Rolling Stone and other media outlets.

item.title: SZA Drops New Song 'Save the Day' for Pixar's 'Hoppers'
item.description: SZA has released her first song since winning a Grammy for Record of the Year earlier this month. The new single is titled “Save the Day," and it appears on the soundtrack to the forthcoming Disney-Pixar film 'Hoppers'.

item.title: Metallica Share Details of Las Vegas Sphere Residency
item.description: After months of speculation, Metallica has confirmed a new residency at the Las Vegas Sphere. The iconic venue will host the metal band’s Life Burns Faster shows across eight dates: October 1, 3, 15, 17, 22, 24, 29, and 31.

item.title: AI Music Guidelines: What Broadcasters Need to Know
item.description: Can you play AI music on internet radio? Learn Live365’s official guidelines for broadcasting AI-generated vs. AI-assisted music and staying copyright compliant.

item.title: Bruno Mars Drops New Album and Shares Music Video for 'Risk It All'
item.description: Bruno Mars’ first record in a decade - and his fourth studio album to date - is out now (February 27). To celebrate the release of The Romantic, Mars has dropped another music video...this time, for his track "Risk It All."

item.title: When We Were Young Festival Cancels 2026 Event
item.description: The beloved pop-punk When We Were Young Festival is taking a hiatus this year. Late last month, the team confirmed on social media the event would be skipping its 2026 edition in order to prioritize a grand return in October 2027.

item.title: Oscars 2026: Ludwig Göransson and HUNTR/X win, Miles Caton,Barbara Streisand, Josh Groban & More Perform
item.description: Ludwig Göransson locked in his third career Oscar win for his work on Sinners, while the ladies behind the fictional K-pop girl group HUNTR/X won "Best Original Song" for the animated Netflix movie KPop Demon Hunters.

item.title: BTS to Make Late Night Comeback on Back-To-Back Episodes of ‘The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon'
item.description: K-pop royalty RM, Jin, SUGA, j-hope, Jimin, V and Jung Kook of BTS will soon reunite on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. The upcoming booking will mark the group's first U.S. late night appearance since all members have completed their mandatory military service.

item.title: 12 Ways to Keep Your Radio Listeners Listening Longer
item.description: In an era of algorithms, your station's human connection is your biggest competitive advantage. Discover 12 practical ways to increase listener engagement and TSL by leaning into authenticity, curation, and that 'live' feel.

item.title: Miley Cyrus Releases New Hannah Montana Song
item.description: If you're one of the many fans who's caught the Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special on Disney+, you'll be pleased to know Miley Cyrus has dropped a brand new song as her famous alter ego.

item.title: Spinning for a Cause: Live365 Powers the Vinylthon 2026 Pop-Up Station
item.description: Celebrate the art of the crate with Live365 and Vinylthon 2026. Discover how we’re powering the WVYL pop-up station and how you can join the 100% vinyl movement.

item.title: Olivia Rodrigo Shares Details of Third Studio Album
item.description: On April 2, the words “you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love” appeared on a pink display located at the corner of Melrose and Sycamore Avenue. Turns out, it's the title of Olivia Rodrigo’s new album: You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love
